Test a cluster count against matched nulls

Source: R/matched_null_test.R
matched_null_test.Rd

Runs the user's own clustering pipeline on the real data and on R matched-null twins of it (see copula_null()), and asks whether the real result exceeds what the twins produce. The twins are a reference model fitted to the data: every twin column is a permutation of the observed values, so the margins are preserved exactly; the correlations are reproduced approximately (see copula_null() for why); and the twins contain no cluster structure by construction. The pipeline is supplied as a function, so any procedure that returns a number, a BIC-selected mixture, a k-means heuristic, a published typology's own workflow, can be tested unchanged.

Usage

matched_null_test(
  x,
  cluster_fn,
  R = 200,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  copula = c("gaussian", "t"),
  df = 8,
  ridge = 1e-06,
  parallel = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or data frame, complete cases only.

cluster_fn

A function taking a data matrix and returning one finite number: the statistic to be tested, typically the selected number of clusters (but any scalar summary of clustering strength works). A return value that is missing, non-finite, non-numeric, or not of length one is an error, on the real data and on every twin.

R

Number of matched-null twins to draw (default 200). The result always holds exactly R twin statistics.

probs

Lower and upper quantiles of the twin statistics that define the reference interval (default c(.025, .975)).

copula, df

Dependence family of the twins and t degrees of freedom, passed to copula_null(). Defaults to "gaussian", which is the reference model of the method; copula = "t" is a sensitivity variant with heavier-tailed dependence, run in addition to the Gaussian test rather than in place of it, and df is fixed by the caller, never estimated from the data.

ridge

Passed to copula_null().

parallel

Evaluate the twin loop through future.apply, so that the backend is whatever future::plan() the caller has set. Because the twins are independent and the null construction itself is a negligible share of the cost, the speed-up is close to the cost of the user's own pipeline divided by the number of workers. Seeded results are reproducible and do not depend on how many workers run them. They do, however, differ from the parallel = FALSE stream, which is left byte-identical to earlier versions, so a seeded analysis should not switch settings partway through.

Value

An object of class "matched_null_test": a list with the real statistic (real), the R twin statistics (null), the reference interval (interval, the probs quantiles of null), the plug-in Monte Carlo exceedance quantity (p_exceed, computed as (1 + sum(null >= real)) / (R + 1); not an exact finite-sample p-value, see Details), whether the real statistic lies inside the interval (within), the requested R, and the reference family used (copula, with df when it is "t"). Reproducibility is the caller's: set a seed before calling.

Details

cluster_fn must return one finite number on every call. If it returns NA, NaN, Inf, a non-numeric value, or a vector of the wrong length, on the real data or on any twin, the test stops with an error naming the offending call. Invalid twins are never dropped and R is never quietly reduced, because an exceedance computed from a subset of the twins would not be the one that was asked for. Errors raised inside cluster_fn propagate unchanged.

p_exceed is a plug-in Monte Carlo exceedance quantity: one plus the number of twins whose statistic reaches the real value, divided by R + 1, under a reference fitted to the same data. It is not an exact finite-sample p-value. The reference's correlations are estimated from x and reproduced only approximately, so p_exceed is a comparison against that fitted reference, not a test with guaranteed size.

Reading the outcome. A real statistic above the twins' interval means the data depart from this reference model, one that carries their margins, approximately their correlations, and no cluster structure. It does not by itself establish that clusters exist: structure the reference does not carry, heavy-tailed dependence included, can produce the same departure, and whether a particular departure registers depends on the statistic, the pipeline and the sample size. A real statistic inside the interval means no detected excess under this reference; it is not evidence that clusters are absent. A statistic below the interval is reported as a diagnostic (the pipeline finds less on the data than on its twins), not as a verdict.

copula = "t" is a sensitivity variant. It gives the twins heavier-tailed dependence at a df fixed by the caller (8, then 3, is a reasonable pair), so a rerun shows whether a departure from the Gaussian twins persists once tail co-movement is built into the reference. A departure that persists is harder to attribute to tails; one that disappears is consistent with tail dependence. Neither outcome by itself establishes or rules out clusters. The Gaussian run is the primary analysis and the t run is reported alongside it, not in its place.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(mclust))
  # a pipeline: how many components does BIC select?
  pick_k <- function(d) Mclust(d, G = 1:5, verbose = FALSE)$G
  set.seed(42)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(500 * 4), 500, 4)  # typeless data
  matched_null_test(x, pick_k, R = 30)

  # sensitivity variant with heavier-tailed dependence in the reference:
  # matched_null_test(x, pick_k, R = 30, copula = "t", df = 8)
}
#> Matched-null test (30 Gaussian null twins)
#>   real statistic:               1
#>   null interval:                [1, 1]
#>   MC exceedance (null >= real): 1
#>   outcome:                      no detected excess (within the reference interval)
# }
